A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe FramePack, with readable, matching core methods and experiments. Both end with references and contain no appendices or embedded supplements. V3 refers to unavailable supplementary benchmarks, ablations, and training details, limiting comparison of those aspects.

before.justification: V1 reports original HunyuanVideo experiments, architectural ablations, automatic quality and drifting measurements, and human preference assessments in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: V3 retains original experimental results and adds discrete-history ablations and DiffusionForcing noise-schedule comparisons in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: V3 adds feature-similarity and hybrid frame ordering, multiple-endpoint planning with different prompts, and K-means codebook discretization of conditioning history during training. These change the conditioning and generation procedures beyond v1's temporal packing and endpoint/inverted sampling.

E1.justification: The supplied results retain general text-to-video and image-to-video coverage. V3 describes additional video-game/world-model evaluations only through references to an unavailable supplement; Section 3.2 also describes evaluation prospectively. The actual extent of added dataset and task coverage cannot be established.

E2.justification: V1 already evaluates noisy history resembling DiffusionForcing. V3 Table 2 expands this comparator into four explicitly evaluated noise-scheduling variants. Repeating image-to-video, anchor frames resembling StreamingT2V, causal attention resembling CausVid, and HistoryGuidance remain, making this a focused expansion within an existing comparator family.

E3.justification: V3 introduces controlled DiffusionForcing settings: randomized training noise with test multipliers 0, 0.1, or 0.5, and fixed training/test multipliers of 0.1. Table 2 also specifies K=256 for discrete history. The existing input counts, video durations, quality metrics, start/end measurement windows, and human-assessment sample requirements remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds matched discrete-history variants testing whether causal generation can reduce drift without future endpoints. Table 2 adds training-versus-inference noise-schedule ablations, substantially extending the investigation of error propagation. Further K-sensitivity analyses are referenced but unavailable and are not credited as inspected evidence.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. ELO-K32 scoring and the stated ±16 tie threshold remain unchanged; revised ELO values and ranks are result changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add discrete-history and noise-scheduling results. All 30 original Table 1 variants retain their automatic scores, while human scores and ranks are revised. Table 2 changes dynamic scores from 65.56% to 91.21% for repeating image-to-video and from 67.56% to 88.27% for causal attention. The new discrete-history candidate shares first human rank with inverted sampling; these additions are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V3 adds mathematical definitions of cosine, temporal, and hybrid importance and codebook quantization in Equations 3–6, without new theorems or proofs. The geometric-series boundedness argument remains, but its shortened limit expression in Section 3.1 incorrectly omits the Lf factor present in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion broaden the contributions to similarity-based packing and discrete-history drift prevention for causal streaming, alongside bidirectional generation. V3 also claims processing thousands of frames with 13B models on 6–8GB GPUs and reduces the earlier emphasis on visual-quality improvements from lower flow shifts.

C2.justification: V3 replaces v1's broad assertion that future-frame access eliminates drift with qualifications concerning limited, periodic, or texture-like motion, and acknowledges possible drift between planned endpoints. It adds a training/inference distribution explanation for discretization and discusses the dynamic-range trade-off between inverted sampling and causal discrete-history generation.

D1.justification: V1 specifies base-model modifications, filtering and resolution buckets, Adafactor settings, gradient clipping, training durations, and Flux flow shifting. These details are absent from the supplied v3, which refers training details to an unavailable supplement. V3 newly specifies LoRA/window-dependent batch capacities and discretization parameters. This materially changes available reproducibility information without establishing changes to the underlying retained experiments.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning around latent compression, including FlexTok, PyramidFlow, and HiTVideo, and around geometric and retrieval-based world-model memory, including WorldMem. It also connects the forgetting/drifting argument to prior error analyses, extending v1's emphasis on long-video generation and efficient architectures.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten and the author list expands. The method section becomes separate packing and drift-prevention sections; packing variants are reorganized, experimental subsections are consolidated, implementation prose is heavily compressed, and related-work organization changes. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is extensively redrawn to contrast temporal and similarity-based ordering and reorganize packing diagrams. Figure 2 expands from three sampling panels to five panels including planned endpoints and discretization. Both tables expand structurally, Table 1 gains a ranking footnote, and the title-page design and typesetting change.

improvement.justification: The discrete-history ablations, expanded noise-scheduling comparison, and narrower endpoint claims strengthen the evidence and interpretation. However, substantial reproducibility details and key new evaluations are deferred to an absent supplement. V3 also says larger K strengthens drift prevention in Section 5.3, conflicting with its K-to-infinity discussion in Section 4.2. These material benefits and shortcomings prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
